title: Auto Loans: when a late charge is PCB's error because the autopay debit went to a closed account
content:
# Auto Loans: when a late charge is PCB's error because the autopay debit went to a closed account

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB decides whether a late charge on an auto loan was assessed contrary to the Auto Loans charter because the installment went unpaid through PCB's own handling of an autopay debit.

## Clause

PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a source account that is open on each debit date, so an installment left unpaid by a debit presented to an account PCB's own records show already closed is left unpaid by PCB's error, not the borrower's.

Accordingly, the late charge is PCB's error when the installment it was charged on went unsatisfied because PCB presented that installment's autopay debit to a PCB checking account closed before the debit's posting date, and the debit came back unpaid. The closing date of the debit's paying account is read from the borrower's checking records and compared with the debit's posting date. It is not PCB's error when no payment reversal names the debit, or when the paying account was still open on the debit's posting date or has no closing date.

## Truth table

| Debit came back unpaid (a reversal names it)? | Paying account's closing date compared with the debit's posting date | PCB's error? |
|---|---|---|
| yes | earlier | yes |
| yes | same day | no |
| yes | later | no |
| yes | no closing date | no |
| no | any | no |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical debit posted 2026-05-05 and returned)

| Paying account closed on | PCB's error? |
|---|---|
| 2026-04-30 | yes |
| 2026-05-05 | no: the account was still open on the posting date |

## Points of judgement

**The borrower says the account was closed; is that enough?** The closing date is taken from PCB's checking records, not from the borrower's account of events.
